newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian partners clear Boddington mine study.
newsitem.headline: Australian partners clear Boddington mine study.

text.p: The joint venture partners in the Boddington gold mine in Western Australia said on Monday they had agreed to commence a full feasibility study for an extended underground operation at the mine.

The joint venture partners, Normandy Mining Ltd (44.44 percent), Acacia Resources Ltd (33.33 percent) and Newcrest Mining Ltd (22.22 percent), said the full study followed the completion of an 18 month pre-feasibility study.

In a joint announcement, the partners said the study would be based on an estimated resource of 311 million tonnes at 0.87 grams per tonne (g/t) gold and 0.10 percent copper and a throughput rate of 11 million tonnes per year.

"The prefeasibility study also established estimates for an initial capital outlay of approximately A$260 million (plus or minus 20 percent), initial gold production of approximately 300,000 ounces per annum at a cash operating cost of A$350 per ounce (after allowance of copper credits at US$1.00/pound), overall gold recovery of 86 percent and copper recovery of 75 to 80 percent," the statement said.

The companies said they expected to consider recommendations before the end of calendar 1997 to permit detailed engineering and the ordering of long lead time items for a plant commissioning in mid-1999.
